title: Joint GKP Encoding for GHZ States Transmission over Bosonic Quantum MIMO Channels
authors: Seid Koudia, Selssabil Kadid, Symeon Chatzinotas, Mérouane Debbah
abstract: We study transmission of a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state over nonunitary quantum multiple-input multiple-output (QuMIMO) channels using finite-energy Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) encoding. A coupled-mode model describes coherent mixing, mode-dependent attenuation, and Gaussian noise. The transceiver combines programmable passive meshes, quantum-limited MMSE gain, local GKP recovery, and joint classical syndrome decoding. We optimize complex-Givens lattices using instantaneous channel-state information (CSI), current singular values with channel statistics, or statistics alone. Simulations show that joint lattice shaping outperforms product GKP processing. Under coherent-basis drift, full instantaneous CSI improves GHZ-state preservation, whereas singular-value conditioned and fully statistical designs perform similarly because neither resolves the current singular frames. These findings identify singular-frame geometry as a critical resource beyond attenuation knowledge where joint GKP processing adapts the logical lattice and receiver to anisotropic bosonic noise rather than merely inverting multimode mixing.
summary: This work develops a joint GKP encoding scheme to protect GHZ states transmitted through noisy bosonic quantum channels. By optimizing the lattice structure based on channel information, the authors show that joint processing adapts to anisotropic noise better than simpler product methods. This advances the understanding of robust quantum communication in complex, realistic quantum network environments.
main_problem: The paper investigates the challenge of transmitting fragile Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states over realistic, nonunitary Quantum Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (QuMIMO) bosonic channels.
main_result: Joint GKP lattice shaping significantly outperforms product GKP processing, demonstrating that adapting the logical lattice to the anisotropic noise geometry is crucial for high-fidelity state preservation.
method: The authors employ a sophisticated transceiver combining programmable passive meshes, quantum-limited MMSE gain, local GKP recovery, and joint classical syndrome decoding.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a bosonic QuMIMO channel governed by a coupled-mode Gaussian evolution equation, incorporating coherent mixing, mode-dependent attenuation, and Gaussian noise.
key_observables: GHZ-state fidelity ($F_{GHZ}$), entanglement fidelity ($	ext{Fe}$), and coherent information ($I_c$) are used to quantify state preservation.
important_parameters: Channel-State Information (CSI) availability (full instantaneous vs. singular-value conditioned vs. statistical) and the degree of coherent basis drift are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The required CSI is assumed to be supplied by an offline channel-estimation stage, and the exact classical Pauli-coset decoding is complex, necessitating structured lattices.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the CSI-aware Gaussian QuMIMO-GKP architecture and show performance metrics (like $F_{GHZ}$) across varying propagation distances, comparing joint vs. product processing schemes.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical model, introduces the GKP encoding/decoding framework, develops optimization functionals based on residual Pauli distributions, and compares performance across different CSI utilization regimes.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, advanced framework for quantum communication over realistic noisy channels, directly addressing resource limitations (like CSI) in quantum networking protocols.
